summary: 来自四个国家的七枚火箭将于本周发射。星际飞船将尝试其迄今为止最重要的任务，而猎鹰 9 号将为美国太空军发射一对机密有效载荷。联合发射联盟计划让 Vulcan 执行其返回飞行任务，而 Electron 则将完成第 100 次任务，具有里程碑意义。在国际上，中国和韩国将分别发射未知的有效载荷和演示任务。猎鹰 9 号 | USSF-627（“R-5”）本周首次发射将由猎鹰 9 号火箭提供机密有效载荷
content:
来自四个国家的七枚火箭将于本周发射。星际飞船将尝试其迄今为止最重要的任务，而猎鹰 9 号将为美国太空军发射一对机密有效载荷。联合发射联盟计划让 Vulcan 执行其返回飞行任务，而 Electron 则将完成第 100 次任务，具有里程碑意义。在国际上，中国和韩国将分别发射未知的有效载荷和演示任务。猎鹰 9 号 | USSF-627（“R-5”）本周首次发射将由猎鹰 9 号火箭为美国太空军 (USSF) 提供机密有效载荷。该任务被指定为 USSF-627，最初计划于 11 月 8 日星期日发射。猎鹰 9 号现定于太平洋标准时间 11 月 9 日星期一晚上 7:07（世界标准时间 10 月 10 日 03:07）从范登堡太空部队基地 (VSFB) 的 4 号东部太空发射综合体 (SLC-4E) 起飞，距太平洋标准时间晚上 11:03 (07:03) 的窗口期已过去四分钟。 UTC 时间 11 月 10 日）。由于有效载荷的机密性质，卫星的确切数量尚不清楚。一些迹象表明，基于猎鹰 9 号第二级的降落区，星盾将进行发射。 Starshield是为美国政府打造的Starlink版本，其主要客户是USSF、国家侦察办公室和太空发展局。范登堡太空部队基地 4E 号航天发射场发射台上的猎鹰 9 号火箭。
（图片来源：SpaceX） Falcon 9 是一款两级、70 m 高、部分可重复使用的火箭，第一级使用九个 Merlin 1D 海平面发动机，第二级使用单个真空优化的 Merlin 1D。Falcon 9 的第一级着陆在自主无人机船上或着陆点，其整流罩在飞行后回收并重复使用。两个阶段都使用液体煤油和液氧作为推进剂。助推器 B1103 将在其第七次飞行中支持这项任务。此前，该助推器已支持 NROL-179、第一批传输层 A 和 E 以及三个星链任务的发射。猎鹰 9 号将搭乘 SpaceX 的无人机“当然我仍然爱你”着陆。米尔 |演示飞行 11 月 10 日星期二，韩国计划发射韩国军方小型卫星运载火箭和平号的第二次飞行。继 2023 年 12 月进行了不包括第二级的试飞之后，此次发射将是全尺寸火箭的首次轨道飞行。启动窗口于 05:00 UTC 开始，并延长至 09:00 UTC。和平号是一款四级固体燃料运载火箭，第四级采用液体燃料，可实现精确入轨。 2023 年 12 月飞行的版本能够运载 700 公斤至近地轨道，该版本疑似能够运载 1,000 公斤左右。长征2D |有效载荷未知 11 月 11 日星期三，长征 2D (CZ-2D) 火箭计划从酒泉卫星发射中心发射升空。
目前，发射计划于 11:40 UTC 进行，距离 11:32 UTC 开启并持续到 12:05 UTC 的窗口还有 8 分钟的时间。CZ-2D 将向轨道发射未知有效载荷。 CZ-2D 是一款两级、41 米高的运载火箭，能够向近地轨道 (LEO) 发射 3,500 公斤的重量。 CZ-2D的第一级和第二级均由四氧化二氮和不对称二甲肼提供动力，这两种推进剂都是自燃推进剂。周三的发射将是长征二号丁的第 107 次发射，也是 2026 年的第六次发射。快舟 11 |有效载荷未知本周第二个也是最后一个预定的中国任务

【原文 English Original】
Seven rockets from four countries are set to launch this week. Starship is set to attempt its most consequential mission yet, while Falcon 9 is set to launch a pair of classified payloads for the United States Space Force. The United Launch Alliance is scheduled to fly Vulcan on its return-to-flight mission, and Electron is set to reach a milestone 100th mission. Internationally, China and South Korea are set to launch an unknown payload and a demonstration mission, respectively. Falcon 9 | USSF-627 (“R-5”) The first launch of the week will feature Falcon 9 delivering a classified payload for the United States Space Force (USSF). The mission, designated USSF-627, was initially scheduled to launch on Sunday, Nov. 8. Falcon 9 is now set to take off from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) on Monday, Nov. 9, at 7:07 PM PST (03:07 UTC on Nov. 10), four minutes into a window that extends until 11:03 PM PST (07:03 UTC on Nov. 10). Due to the classified nature of the payload, the exact quantity of satellites is unknown. Some indicators suggest a Starshield launch, based on drop zones for Falcon 9’s second stage. Starshield is a version of Starlink built for the United States government, with its primary customers being the USSF, National Reconnaissance Office, and the Space Development Agency. A Falcon 9 on the launch pad at Space Launch Complex-4E on Vandenberg Space Force Base. (Credit: SpaceX) Falcon 9 is a two-stage, 70 m-tall, partially reusable rocket that uses nine Merlin 1D sea-level engines on its first stage and a single vacuum-optimized Merlin 1D on its second stage. Falcon 9’s first stage lands either aboard an autonomous droneship or at a landing site, with its fairings being recovered and reused after flight. Both stages utilize liquid kerosene and liquid oxygen as propellants. Booster B1103 will be supporting this mission on its seventh flight. Previously, this booster has supported the launches of NROL-179, Tranche 1 Transport Layers A and E, and three Starlink missions. Falcon 9 will land downrange aboard SpaceX’s droneship Of Course I Still Love You . Mir | Demo Flight On Tuesday, Nov. 10, South Korea is set to launch the second flight of Mir, the South Korean military’s small satellite launch vehicle. This launch is set to be the first orbital flight of the full-scale rocket, following a test flight in December 2023 that did not include the second stage. The launch window opens at 05:00 UTC and extends until 09:00 UTC. Mir is a four-stage, solid-fuel launch vehicle with a liquid-fueled fourth stage for precise orbital insertion. The version that flew in December 2023 was capable of 700 kg to LEO, with this version suspected to be capable of around 1,000 kg. Chang Zheng 2D | Unknown Payload On Wednesday, Nov. 11, a Chang Zheng 2D (CZ-2D) rocket is scheduled to launch out of the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center. The launch is currently scheduled for 11:40 UTC, eight minutes into a window that opens at 11:32 UTC and extends until 12:05 UTC. CZ-2D will deliver an unknown payload into orbit. CZ-2D is a two-stage, 41 m-tall launch vehicle capable of delivering 3,500 kg to low-Earth orbit (LEO). CZ-2D’s first and second stages are both powered by dinitrogen tetroxide and unsymmetrical dimethyl hydrazine, both hypergolic propellants. Wednesday’s launch will be the 107th overall for CZ-2D, and sixth in 2026. Kuaizhou 11 | Unknown Payload The second and final scheduled Chinese mission of the week will see a Kuaizhou 11 rocket launch on Thursday, Nov. 12. Liftoff is set for 19:50 UTC from Site 95A at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, during a 45-minute launch window. Kuaizhou 11 is a four-stage Chinese rocket manufactured by the China Aerospace Science and Industry Corporation. Standing 25.3 m tall, the rocket can loft 1,500 kg to LEO with a liftoff thrust of 1,250 kN. This mission will be the eighth overall Kuaizhou 11 mission and the fourth of 2026. Vulcan VC6L | Amazon Leo (LV-01) United Launch Alliance’s (ULA) Vulcan rocket is set to launch on Friday, Nov. 13, from Space Launch Complex 41 (SLC-41) at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. The 30-minute launch window opens at 12:54 PM EST (17:54 UTC). This will be the first flight of Vulcan in over nine months, following the ejection of one of Vulcan’s GEM-63XL solid rocket boosters at T+69 seconds on the USSF-87 mission. Flying aboard Vulcan will be a stack of 40 Amazon Leo satellites for Amazon’s Leo satellite internet constellation, a rival to SpaceX’s Starlink. A ULA Vulcan (USSF-87) sits next to a SpaceX Crew Dragon (Crew-12). (Credit: Tyler Gray for NSF) Vulcan is a two-stage launch vehicle with a range of launch configurations. Vulcan’s first stage is powered by two BE-4 engines built by Blue Origin, running on liquid methane and liquid oxygen propellants. Its second stage, Centaur V, is powered by twin RL10C engines running on liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen. Centaur V can be configured as Centaur LEO, High Energy, or Endurance. Vulcan can also be configured with solid rocket boosters to augment liftoff thrust, with options ranging from zero to two, four, or six boosters. The payload is encapsulated by either a short (15.5 m) or a long (21.3 m) fairing. Vulcan will debut the Vulcan VC6L variant, designated by six solid boosters and the long fairing option. Vulcan will debut the LEO-optimized Centaur V, which is 1.94 m smaller than the existing Centaur V High Energy, which has flown on all previous Vulcan launches. Additionally, this flight is a certification flight of this Vulcan configuration for the United States Space Force. Amazon Leo (LV-01) will be the first of 38 scheduled for Vulcan and the fifth overall mission for Vulcan. Starship | Flight 15 / Starlink Group 31-2 Pending regulatory approval, Starship is set to fly its next, and most significant, mission no earlier than Friday, Nov. 13, at 4:45 PM CST (22:45 UTC). The launch window extends until 6:00 PM CST (00:00 UTC on Nov. 14). Flight 15 will feature two notable events: the first booster-catch attempt since Flight 8, following stage separation, and the first attempt to catch the ship, roughly 22 hours after liftoff. Starship is a two-stage, super-heavy-lift launch vehicle capable of lofting an estimated 100 tonnes. The first stage, named Super Heavy, features 33 Raptor 3 engines, running off of liquid methane and liquid oxygen propellants. The second stage, named Starship, features six Raptor 3 engines, three sea-level and three vacuum-optimized, also running off of liquid methane and liquid oxygen. Flying on Flight 15 will be Ship 42 and Booster 22, both on their first flights. Flight 15 is expected to deliver 26 Starlink v3 satellites to LEO. Like Flight 14, three of these satellites will feature imaging capabilities for imaging the heat shield of Starship in orbit. Flight 15 will be the 15th full-stack launch of Starship and the fourth for the system’s V3 configuration. Falcon 9 | USSF-317 (“R-6”) Falcon 9 is set to fly again on Friday, Nov. 13, from VSFB with another USSF mission. The designation for this flight is USSF-317. The launch window opens at 8:09 PM PST (04:09 UTC on Nov. 14), and lasts for four hours. This mission will fly another unknown quantity of presumed Starshield satellites to LEO. Booster B1100 will support this mission, marking its 11th flight. This booster has previously supported NROL-105, USSF-385, and eight Starlink missions. B1100 will land downrange aboard SpaceX’s droneship Of Course I Still Love You . Electron during its 95th launch “Happily Ever Faster.” Credit: Rocket Lab) Electron | The Mountain God Rises The last scheduled launch of the week will see Rocket Lab’s Electron launch from the Mahia Peninsula in New Zealand on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 05:30 UTC. This flight of Electron, named “The Mountain God Rises,” will deliver another iQPS satellite into LEO for iQPS’s synthetic aperture radar constellation (SAR). SAR is used to image the surface of the Earth and can penetrate through cloud layers. Electron is a two-stage small-lift vehicle capable of delivering up to 300 kg to LEO and 200 kg to Sun-synchronous orbit. The vehicle is fueled by liquid kerosene and liquid oxygen, which powers nine Rutherford engines on the first stage and a single vacuum-optimized Rutherford on the second stage. This mission will serve as Electron’s 100th overall mission — a notable milestone for the small rocket that first flew in 2017. In addition, this mission will serve as the 269th orbital launch attempt worldwide in 2026. ( Lead Image: Falcon 9 launches from Florida. Credit: Julia Bergeron for NSF) The post Launch Preview: Starship, Vulcan, and Electron launches scheduled for busy week appeared first on NASASpaceFlight.com .

content:
资助机会通知 (NOFO)：在斯威士兰举办 2027 GCTF 研讨会 资助机会通知 (NOFO) 在斯威士兰美国台湾学院举办 2027 G CTF 研讨会 机会编号：GCTF-TAIPEI-FY2 7 -00 1 申请截止日期：202 年 11 月 23 日 6 日晚上 11:59 （台北时间） A. 基本信息 1. 概述 资助方式：合作协议。合作协议包括局或大使馆实质性参与项目的计划实施。实质性参与的例子包含在下面的 C.2 节中。项目实施期限：拟建项目应于202年5月31日前完成 7．本通知视资金情况而定。公共外交部门保留在被认为符合美国政府最佳利益的情况下授予少于或超过所述资金的权利，具体取决于资金的可用性和指定拨款官员的批准。 2. 执行摘要 美国在台协会 (AIT) 公共外交部门 (PDS) 宣布开展一项合作协议公开竞赛，以支持 2027 年第一季度或第二季度在斯威士兰规划和实施全球合作与培训框架 (GCTF) 区域特许经营研讨会。在资金允许的情况下，AIT 打算授予一份约 20 万美元的合作协议来实施该计划。
全球合作与培训框架（GCTF）是一个国际能力建设平台，汇集了政府官员、技术专家、行业代表、学者和民间社会代表，交流实践经验并加强应对区域和全球挑战的合作。GCTF由台湾和美国于2015年成立，此后扩大到包括日本、澳大利亚、加拿大和英国作为合作伙伴。拟议的研讨会“加强南部非洲的网络安全和数字治理”预计将于 2027 年第一季度或第二季度在斯威士兰举行。该计划将重点关注加强网络安全弹性、改善数字治理、保护关键数字基础设施、应对新出现的网络威胁以及促进安全和可信的数字转型。它将为参与者提供一个交流实践经验、确定共同挑战、加强专业网络和区域合作的平台。该研讨会预计将包括来自至少八个非洲国家的代表，特别强调南部非洲的区域参与。第一天预计将有约 60 至 80 名参与者参加，活动内容包括全体讨论、专家演讲和实践交流。
预计第二天将有约 40 名参与者参加，其中可能包括重点技术讨论、互动练习、工作组会议和/或相关现场参观。该计划预计将汇集来自参与非洲国家的政府官员、网络安全和数字治理从业者、技术专家、私营部门代表、学者、民间社会代表和其他相关利益攸关方。来自美国、台湾和其他 GCTF 合作伙伴（包括日本、澳大利亚、加拿大）的主题专家

Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO): Implementation of 2027 GCTF Workshop in Eswatini Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) Implementation of 2027 G CTF Workshop in Eswatini American Institute in Taiwan Opportunity number: GCTF-TAIPEI-FY2 7 -00 1 Application deadline: November 23 , 202 6 , at 11:59 p.m. (Taipei Time)   A. Basic Information 1. Overview Funding Instrument Type: C ooperative agreement . Cooperative agreements include substantial involvement of the bureau or embassy in program implementation of the project. Examples of substantial involvement are included in section C.2 below. Project Performance Period : Proposed projects should be completed by May 31 , 202 7 . This notice is subject to availability of funding. The Public Diplomacy Section reserves the right to award less or more than the funds described under circumstances deemed to be in the best interest of the U.S. government, pending the availability of funds and approval of the designated grants officer. 2. Executive Summary The American Institute in Taiwan (AIT) Public Diplomacy Section (PDS) announces an open competition for a cooperative agreement to support the planning and implementation of a Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) regional franchise workshop in Eswatini in the first or second quarter of 2027. Subject to the availability of funding, AIT intends to award one cooperative agreement of approximately USD 200,000 to implement this program. The Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) is an international capacity-building platform that brings together government officials, technical experts, industry representatives, academics, and civil society representatives to exchange practical experiences and strengthen cooperation in addressing regional and global challenges. The GCTF was established by Taiwan and the United States in 2015 and has since expanded to include Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom as Partners. The proposed workshop, “Strengthening Cybersecurity and Digital Governance in Southern Africa,” is expected to take place in Eswatini during the first or second quarter of 2027. The program will focus on strengthening cybersecurity resilience, improving digital governance, protecting critical digital infrastructure, addressing emerging cyber threats, and promoting secure and trusted digital transformation. It will provide a platform for participants to exchange practical experiences, identify common challenges, and strengthen professional networks and regional cooperation. The workshop is expected to include representatives from at least eight African countries, with a particular emphasis on regional participation from Southern Africa. Approximately 60 to 80 participants are expected to participate in the first day of the program, which will feature plenary discussions, expert presentations, and practical exchanges. A smaller group of approximately 40 participants is expected to participate in the second day, which may include focused technical discussions, interactive exercises, working-group sessions, and/or relevant site visits. The program is expected to bring together government officials, cybersecurity and digital governance practitioners, technical experts, private-sector representatives, academics, civil society representatives, and other relevant stakeholders from participating African countries. Subject-matter experts from the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF Partners, including Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom, may also be invited to contribute relevant international expertise and practical experience. The selected recipient will serve as AIT’s implementation partner and will be responsible for comprehensive program and logistical support, including venue and lodging coordination, participant management, travel arrangements for designated participants and speakers, ground transportation, interpretation and audiovisual services, workshop materials, vendor coordination, monitoring and evaluation, and required grant reporting. Travel expenses for U.S. Government officials invited by the U.S. Government and Taiwan-supported speakers will be funded separately and should not be included in the recipient’s proposed budget. AIT and GCTF partners will provide overall policy guidance, strategic direction, and substantive oversight throughout program planning and implementation. Eligible applicants include nonprofit organizations, educational institutions, professional associations, think tanks, private-sector organizations with relevant international program management experience, public international organizations where eligible under applicable U.S. Government regulations, and other eligible organizations with demonstrated capacity to organize international conferences or capacity-building programs and administer U.S. Government assistance awards. This cooperative agreement is intended to strengthen practical cybersecurity capacity and digital governance cooperation in Southern Africa, expand professional and institutional connections among participating countries, and advance the GCTF as a platform for practical international capacity building, technical exchange, and sustained regional cooperation. B. Eligibility 1. Eligible Applicants The following organizations are eligible to apply: Not-for-profit organizations , including non-governmental organizations (NGOs), think tanks, and civil society organizations Educational institutions , including universities and research institutions Professional associations and nonprofit organizations with demonstrated experience managing international conferences or capacity-building programs Private-sector organizations with demonstrated experience organizing international conferences or implementing international exchange programs Public international organizations , where eligible under applicable U.S. Government regulations Organizations may sub-contract with other entities, but only one entity, from the eligible categories of organizations listed above, can be the prime recipient of the award. When sub-contracting with other entities, the responsibilities of each entity must be clearly defined in the proposal. For more information on the difference between sub-contract and sub-recipient, please refer to 2 CFR 200 .331 . 2. Cost Sharing or Matching Cost sharing is not required . 3. Other Eligibility Requirements All organizations must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) issued via SAM.gov as well as a valid registration in SAM.gov. Please see Section D.3 for more information. Individuals are not required to have a UEI or be registered in SAM.gov. Applicants are only allowed to submit one proposal per organization. If more than one proposal is submitted from an organization, all proposals from that institution will be considered ineligible for funding. 4. This opportunity will not support: Projects relating to partisan political activity; Charitable or development activities; including direct social services such as medical, psychological, and/or humanitarian support Construction projects; Projects that support specific religious activities; Fund-raising campaigns; Lobbying for specific legislation or programs Scientific research or surveys; Commercial projects; Projects intended primarily for the growth or institutional development of the organization; Projects that duplicate existing projects; Illegal activities C. Program Description 1. Project Background, Goals, and Objectives Project Background The Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) is an international capacity-building platform established by Taiwan and the United States in 2015. Japan joined as a full partner in 2019, followed by Australia in 2021, Canada in 2023, and the United Kingdom in 2025. Through workshops and other capacity-building activities, GCTF brings together government officials, technical experts, industry representatives, and civil society representatives to exchange practical experience, strengthen professional networks, and develop approaches to shared regional and global challenges. As governments and societies become increasingly dependent on digital technologies and interconnected systems, cybersecurity and effective digital governance have become important elements of economic development, public-service delivery, critical infrastructure resilience, and public trust. Recent research documents that scam syndicates displaced from Southeast Asian epicenters, including Myanmar, Laos, and Cambodia, are actively pivoting to Africa, with documented raids in nine African countries and growing evidence of scam infrastructure, including online gambling platforms used as cover for fraud operations, gray business Telegram groups openly advertising scam facilities, and unregulated cryptocurrency services establishing footholds across the continent. Countries across Southern Africa face evolving cybersecurity and cybercrime challenges while also seeking to expand digital services, strengthen institutional capacity, and develop governance frameworks that support secure and trusted digital transformation. The proposed GCTF regional workshop in Eswatini will provide a platform for government officials, cybersecurity and the digital governance practitioners, technical experts, private-sector representatives, academics, civil society representatives, and other relevant stakeholders from across Africa to exchange practical experiences and strengthen professional and institutional connections. The workshop is expected to include representatives from at least eight African countries, with particular emphasis on participation from Southern Africa. The program will draw on expertise and practical experience from participating African countries as well as the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF partners, as appropriate. Through expert presentations, policy and technical discussions, interactive exchanges, and other practical activities, the workshop will address shared challenges and identify approaches that participating countries may adapt to their respective national and institutional contexts. Strengthening cybersecurity capacity and secure digital governance in Southern Africa also advances U.S. security and economic interests. Cyber threats, cyber-enabled crime, and vulnerabilities in interconnected digital systems increasingly cross-national borders and can affect American citizens, businesses, and critical infrastructure. By strengthening the ability of partner countries to prevent, identify, respond to, and recover from cyber threats, this program can help reduce vulnerabilities that may be exploited by transnational criminal networks and other malicious cyber actors. The workshop will also strengthen U.S. engagement with African partners on secure and resilient digital ecosystems, promote cooperation and information sharing among governments and technical experts, and expand relationships between African stakeholders and the United States and other GCTF partners. Through practical capacity building and sustained professional networks, the program will support a more secure and resilient regional digital environment while advancing shared interests in cybersecurity, economic security, and trusted digital development. Project Goal: The goal of this project is to strengthen cybersecurity resilience and digital governance capacity in Southern Africa by facilitating practical knowledge exchange, regional cooperation, and sustained professional engagement among participating countries and international partners, while advancing shared U.S. and partner interests in a more secure, resilient, and trusted digital environment. Project Objectives: The project will pursue the following objectives: Strengthen Cybersecurity Capacity and Resilience: Enhance participants’ knowledge of practical approaches to preventing, preparing for, responding to, and recovering from cybersecurity threats and incidents, with a specific focus on basic cyber hygiene, national cyber resilience, digital trust, and the development of a secure digital ecosystem aligned with global standards and best practices. Advance Effective and Secure Digital Governance: Promote the exchange of policies, practices, institutional approaches, and lessons learned that support secure, trusted, resilient, and inclusive digital governance and digital transformation. Promote Regional Cooperation and Information Sharing: Strengthen professional and institutional connections among participating African countries and encourage greater cross-border cooperation, information sharing, and coordination in addressing shared cybersecurity and digital governance challenges. Facilitate Practical International Exchange: Connect African policymakers and practitioners with relevant expertise and practical experience from participating African countries, the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF partner countries, including Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom, as appropriate to the workshop agenda. Support Sustainable Professional Networks and Follow-on Cooperation: Encourage participants to identify practical opportunities for continued professional engagement, knowledge sharing, and future cooperation beyond the workshop. 2. Substantial Involvement This award will require substantial involvement from the American Institute in Taiwan (AIT ) and the U . S . Embassy in Eswatini . AIT will approve all key aspects of the workshop, including but not limited to venue selection, flight and hotel arrangements, ground transportation, lodging, visual designs, agenda, site visit locations, speaker and participant lists, catering and menus, conference room layout, lighting, and audio-visual setup. D. Application Contents and Format Please follow all instructions below carefully. Proposals that do not meet the requirements of this announcement or fail to comply with the stated requirements will be ineligible. Content of Application Please ensure: The proposal clearly addresses the goals and objectives of this funding opportunity All documents are in English All budgets are in U.S. dollars All pages are numbered, including budgets and attachments All documents are formatted to fit 8 ½ x 11 paper All documents are single-spaced, 14-point New Times Roman font, with 1-inch margins. Captions and footnotes may be 10-point New Times Roman font. Font sizes in charts and tables, including the budget, can be reformatted to fit within 1 page width. All applicant authorized signatures are provided where indicated on the various, required forms. The following documents are required: 1. Mandatory application forms SF-424 (Application for Federal Assistance – organizations) at https://grants.gov/ or https://www.ait.org.tw / . SF-424A (Budget Information for Non-Construction programs) at https://grants.gov/ or https://www.ait.org.tw / . SF-424B (Assurances for Non-Construction programs) at https://grants.gov/ or https://www.ait.org.tw / . (note: the SF-424B is only required for individuals, organizations exempt from registration, and for organizations not required to fully register in https://sam.gov/ ) 2. Proposal (10 pages maximum) The proposal should contain sufficient information that anyone not familiar with it would understand exactly what the applicant wants to do. You may use your own proposal format, but it must include all the items below. Proposal Summary: Short narrative that outlines the proposed project, including project objectives and anticipated impact. (Attachment: Recommended Proposal Template ). Introduction to the Organization : A description of past and present operations, showing ability to carry out the program, including information on all previous grants from the State Department and/or U.S. government agencies as well as experience with and expertise in areas related to those described in the NOFO. Applicants are encouraged, but not required, to use the attached Applicant Organization Information Survey form to provide this information (Attachment : Recommended Applicant Organization Information (AOI) Survey Template ). If the applicant chooses not to use the attached form, all of the requested information from the form will still need to be addressed in the application package. Problem Statement: Clear, concise and well-supported statement of the problem to be addressed and why the proposed program is needed Program Methods, Design, Activities, and Deliverables: The “goals” describe what the program is intended to achieve. The “objectives” refer to the intermediate accomplishments on the way to the goals. These should be achievable and measurable. Describe the program activities and how they will help achieve the objectives. Proposed Project Schedule and Timeline: The proposed timeline for the program activities. Include the dates, times, and locations of planned activities and events. Key Personnel: Names, titles, roles and experience/qualifications of key personnel involved in the program. What proportion of their time will be used in support of this program? Project Partners: List the names and type of involvement of key partner organizations and sub-awardees (if applicable). Future Funding or Sustainability: Applicant’s plan for continuing the program beyond the grant period, or the availability of other resources, if applicable. Monitoring & Evaluation Plan: Proposals must include a draft Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Performance Monitoring Plan (PMP). The M&E PMP should show how applicants intend to measure and demonstrate progress towards the project’s objectives and goals. The key components to the PMP are as follows: Monitoring and Evaluation Narrative: In narrative form, applicants should describe how they intend to monitor and evaluate the activities of their award. In addition, the applicant should describe any M&E processes, including key personnel, management structure (where M&E fits into the overall program’s staff structure), technology, and as well provide a brief budget narrative explaining any line-item expenditures for M&E listed in the program’s budget. If the proposal is from a prior grantee, the proposal discusses how the grantee has adapted, improved or otherwise modified their approach based on learning from previous experience. This narrative is limited to two pages. Theory of Change Diagram: Applicants are expected to submit either a Theory of Change diagram or an If-Then Statement that illustrates how project activities will lead to intended outcomes. Monitoring and Evaluation Datasheet: The applicant must include their proposed activities and their expected outputs and outcomes as well as the goals and objectives as written in the NOFO. The datasheet’s purpose is to explicitly illustrate how a project’s activities lead to tangible results (such as increased beneficiary skills, knowledge, or attitudes) that ultimately address a PDS objective. The selected applicant’s M&E PMP is subject to review and approval before any award will be issued under this NOFO. The selected applicant will be required to work with the Public Diplomacy Section’s Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist to ensure the applicant’s M&E PMP achieves an expected level of expertise and meets PDS objectives. Expenses directly associated with monitoring and evaluation are considered allowable. The suggested template includes a space to list the portion of the total budget amount directly associated with monitoring and evaluation activities. 3. Budget Justification Narrative Detailed Budget – Applicants must submit a detailed line-item budget. Applicants are encouraged to utilize the template provided with the funding opportunity but are not required to do so (Attachment: Recommended Budget Narrative Template ). Line-item expenditures should be listed in the greatest possible detail. The budget must identify the total amount of funding requested, with a breakdown of amounts to be spent in the following budget categories: personnel; fringe benefits; travel; equipment; supplies; consultants/contracts; other direct costs; and indirect costs. See Annex Section I for a description of the types of costs that should be included in each category. Personnel salaries should include the level of effort and the rate of pay, which should cover the percentage of time each staff member will dedicate to grant-based activities. If an organization is charging an indirect cost rate without a NICRA, it must apply it to the modified total budget costs (MTDC), refer to 2CFR § 200.1 . Budgets shall be submitted in U.S. dollars and final grant agreements will be conducted in U.S. dollars. Budget Justification Narrative – Applicants must submit a budget justification narrative to accompany the detailed line-item budget. The purpose of the budget justification narrative is to supplement the information provided in the detailed budget spreadsheet by justifying how the budget cost elements are necessary to implement project objectives and accomplish the project goals. The budget justification narrative is a tool to help AIT staff fully understand the budgetary needs of the applicant and is an opportunity to provide descriptive information about the requested costs beyond the constraints of the budget template. Together, the detailed budget spreadsheet, the budget justification narrative, and the SF-424A should provide a complete financial and qualitative description that supports the proposed project plan and should be directly relatable to the specific project components described in the applicant’s proposal. Additional Budget Notes: Curing venues, managing logistics, catering, etc. are allowable. Audit Requirements: Please note the audit requirements for Department of State awards in the Standard Terms and Conditions https://www.state.gov/federal-assistance-policies-appeals, Subpart F – Audit Requirements. The cost of the required audits may be charged either as an allowable direct cost to the award OR included in the organization’s established indirect costs in the award’s detailed budget. Visa Fees: Include all visa application and related fees in your budget as applicable. Please note DS-2019s for post-funded programs must be submitted directly by the award recipient. If you anticipate your program will include the DS-2019 visa processing, your organization must be a registered Designated Sponsoring Organization. For more information go to: https://j1visa.state.gov/sponsors/become-a-sponsor/ 4. Attachments Key Personnel Resumes : A résumé, not to exceed one page in length, must be included for the proposed key staff persons, such as the Project Director and Finance Officer, as well as any speakers or trainers (if applicable). If an individual for this type of position has not been identified, the applicant may submit a 1-page position description, identifying the qualifications and skills required for that position, in lieu of a résumé. Letters of support from program partners: Letters of support should be included for sub-recipients or other partners. The letters must identify the type of relationship to be entered into (formal or informal), the roles and responsibilities of each partner in relation to the proposed project activities, and the expected result of the partnership. The individual letters cannot exceed 1 page in length. Indirect Costs : If your organization has a Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA) and includes NICRA charges in the budget, your latest NICRA should be included in the application submission. Proof of Non-profit Status: Documentation to demonstrate the applicant’s non-profit status (e.g., U.S.-based organizations should submit a copy of their 501(c)(3) Internal Revenue Service determination letter, and non-U.S. organizations should provide evidence of non-profit status issued by a government entity). Proof of Registration: A copy of the organization’s registration should be provided with the proposal application. U.S.-based organizations should submit a copy of their IRS determination letter. Taiwan -based organizations should submit a copy of their certificate of registration from the appropriate government organization. Other items NOT required/requested with the application submission, but which may be requested if your application is approved to move forward in the review process include: Copies of an organization or program audit within the last two (2) years Copies of relevant human resources, financial, or procurement policies Copies of other relevant organizational policies or documentation that would help the Department determine your organization’s capacity to manage a federal grant award overseas Documentation that demonstrates the recipients’ plan and/or policy to safeguard PII of participants and beneficiaries. It is the responsibility of the recipient to ensure protection of personally identifiable information (PII) and safeguard PII when collecting, maintaining, using and disseminating such information Information to determine what financial controls and standard operating procedures an organization uses to procure goods and services, hire staff and track time and attendance, pay for grant-related travel, and identify other financial transactions that may be necessary to undertake the project activities AIT reserves the right to request any additional programmatic and/or financial information regarding the proposal. E. Submission Requirements and Deadlines 1.Address to Request Application Package Application forms required above are available at https://www.ait.org.tw/ , grants.gov, MyGrants, etc. 2.Department of State Contacts If you have any questions about the grant application process, please contact: AITGCTF@state.gov . Question Deadline: For questions on this solicitation, please contact AITGCTF@state.gov . Questions must be received before October 28, 2026 , at 23:59 p.m. (Taipei Time) . Applicants should not expect an email response to questions, as questions received before the deadline will be answered in a question-and-answer document and posted at http://www.grants.gov and https://www.ait.org.tw/ . 3.Unique entity identifier and System for Award Management (SAM.gov) Required Registration: All organizations, whether based in the United States or in another country, must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and an active registration in SAM.gov. A UEI is one of the data elements mandated by Public Law 109-282, the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act (FFATA), for all Federal awards. An applicant must maintain an active registration while it has a proposal under review by the Department and must continue to keep the registration active for the entire duration of the period of performance of any Federal award that results from this NOFO. The 2 CFR 200 also requires subrecipients to obtain a UEI. Please note the UEI for subrecipients is not required at the time of application but will be required before an award is processed and/or directed to a subrecipient. Note: The process of obtaining or renewing a SAM.gov registration may take anywhere from 4-8 weeks. Please begin your registration as early as possible . Organizations based in the United States or that pay employees within the United States will need an Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and a UEI prior to registering in SAM.gov. Organizations based outside of the United States and that do not pay employees within the United States do not need an EIN from the IRS but do need a UEI prior to registering in SAM.gov. Organizations based outside of the United States that do not intend to apply for U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) awards are no longer required to have a NATO Commercial and Government Entity (NCAGE) code to apply for non-DoD foreign assistance funding opportunities. If an applicant organization is mid-registration and wishes to remove an NCAGE code from their SAM.gov registration, the applicant should submit a help desk ticket (“incident”) with the Federal Service Desk (FSD) online at www.fsd.gov using the following language: “I do not intend to seek financial assistance from the Department of Defense. I do not wish to obtain an NCAGE code. I understand that I will need to submit my registration after this incident is resolved in order to have my registration activated.” Organizations based outside of the United States and that DO NOT plan to do business with the DoD should follow the below instructions: Step 1: Proceed to SAM.gov to obtain a UEI and complete the SAM.gov registration process. SAM.gov registration must be renewed annually. Exemptions An exemption from the UEI and sam.gov registration requirements may be permitted on a case-by-case basis. See 2 CFR 25.110 for a full list of exemptions. Organizations requesting exemption from UEI or SAM.gov requirements must email the point of contact listed in the NOFO at least two weeks prior to the deadline in the NOFO providing a justification of their request. Approval for a SAM.gov exemption must come from the warranted Grants Officer before the application can be deemed eligible for review. Please note : Any applicant with an exclusion in the System for Award Management (SAM) is not eligible to apply for an assistance award in accordance with the OMB guidelines at 2 CFR 180 that implement Executive Orders 12549 (3 CFR, 1986 Comp., p. 189) and 12689 (3 CFR, 1989 Comp., p. 235), “Debarment and Suspension.”   4.Submission Dates and Times Submission Deadline: All applications must be received by November 23 , 2026 , at 23:59 p.m. ( Taipei Time ) . content:
2026 年 11 月 13 日

日本横须贺——

由军事海运司令部运营的远征快速运输舰俾斯麦市号（EPF 9）迎来了新任指挥官，中校。蒂亚·迈尔斯在横须贺舰队活动船上举行的仪式上。迈尔斯从中校手中接过指挥权。 VanAnh McCormick，在将该船移交给 MILCREW II 之前担任军事船员 I 的指挥官。

“从我们的人员流动开始，我们不再是 MILCREW II 和 CIVMAR；我们都是俾斯麦市号航空母舰，”迈尔斯在向由水手和公务员组成的混合船员发表的讲话中说道。 “‘保持媒体报道’是我们的全部工作！我们必须在场并准备好参与，同时互相支持，以确保我们的成功。Crew I 奠定了基础，我们的工作就是在此基础上继续发展。Possumus Efficiemus：我们可以而且我们将会实现。”

迈尔斯是南卡罗来纳州哥伦比亚人，2014 年从弗朗西斯马里恩大学毕业并获得数学学士学位后，被任命为海军军官。她还拥有海军研究生院的高级工商管理硕士学位。

在海上，迈尔斯曾在阿利伯克号航空母舰 (DDG 51)、珍珠港号航空母舰 (LSD 52) 和哈珀斯渡口号航空母舰 (LSD 49) 上服役。
在岸上，她在圣地亚哥海军水面和水雷作战发展中心和水面高级作战学校担任两栖作战战术教官。迈尔斯接替了麦考密克，麦考密克于 2026 年 7 月接管了 MILCREW I 的指挥权，并带领船员完成了有史以来的首次 EPF 部署。部署期间，船员航行超过4000海里，访问了4个海外港口。机组人员为“锐剑”演习提供了后勤保障，并完成了任务要求的所有准备工作。此外，供应部门还入围了 David M. Cook 食品服务卓越奖的决赛。

俾斯麦号是EPF级第九艘舰艇。这些浅吃水、全铝制商用双体船旨在以 35 节的平均速度将 600 短吨军用货物运输 1,200 海里。该船设有用于直升机操作的飞行甲板、车辆卸载坡道部署以及增强沿海操作和港口通道的浅吃水。这些能力使 EPF 能够在严峻或受损的港口提供灵活的物流支持、快速运输和救灾。

该船的船员由军事人员和文职海员组成。 MILCREW 轮流部署，基地设在圣地亚哥，而该舰的母港是横须贺，由美国第七舰队负责作战控制。
军事海运司令部负责指挥和支持大约 140 艘民用船只的行动，这些船只为美国海军舰船补充海上补给、执行专门任务、在全球范围内预置战斗货物、提供支持服务以及向部署的美国部队运输军事装备和补给品。

【原文 English Original】
13 November 2026

YOKOSUKA, Japan --

The expeditionary fast transport USS City of Bismarck (EPF 9), operated by Military Sealift Command, welcomed its new commanding officer, Lt. Cmdr. Tia Myers, during a ceremony aboard the ship at Fleet Activities Yokosuka. Myers assumed command from Lt. Cmdr. VanAnh McCormick, who served as the Military Crew I commander before turning the ship over to MILCREW II.

“Starting with our turnover, we are no longer MILCREW II and CIVMARs; we are all USS City of Bismarck,” Myers said in her address to the hybrid crew of sailors and civil service mariners. “It is all of our job to ‘keep the press!’ We have to be present and ready to engage while supporting each other to ensure our success. Crew I laid the foundation, and it is our job to build upon it. Possumus Efficiemus: We can and we will accomplish.”

A native of Columbia, South Carolina, Myers commissioned as a naval officer in 2014 after graduating from Francis Marion University with a bachelor’s degree in mathematics. She also holds an executive master’s degree in business administration from the Naval Postgraduate School.

At sea, Myers served aboard USS Arleigh Burke (DDG 51), USS Pearl Harbor (LSD 52) and USS Harpers Ferry (LSD 49).

Ashore, she served as an amphibious warfare tactics instructor at the Naval Surface and Mine Warfighting Development Center and Surface Advanced Warfighting School in San Diego. Myers relieved McCormick, who took command of MILCREW I in July 2026 and led the crew through its first ever EPF deployment. During the deployment, the crew sailed more than 4,000 nautical miles and visited four overseas ports. The crew provided logistics support for Exercise Keen Sword and completed all ready for tasking requirements. In addition, the supply department became a finalist for the David M. Cook Food Service Excellence Award.

Bismarck is the ninth ship in the EPF class. These shallow-draft, all-aluminum, commercial-based catamarans are designed to transport 600 short tons of military cargo 1,200 nautical miles at an average speed of 35 knots. The ship features a flight deck for helicopter operations, a vehicle offload ramp deployment, and a shallow draft that enhances littoral operations and port access. These capabilities allow the EPF to deliver flexible logistics support, rapid transport and disaster relief in austere or damaged ports.

The ship operates with a hybrid crew of military personnel and civil service mariners. The MILCREWs rotate for deployments and are based in San Diego, while the ship is homeported in Yokosuka under the operational control of U.S. 7th Fleet.

Military Sealift Command directs and supports operations for approximately 140 civilian-crewed ships that replenish U.S. Navy ships at sea, conduct specialized missions, preposition combat cargo worldwide, provide support services, and transport military equipment and supplies to deployed U.S. forces.

summary: 台湾原住民农民重振气候适应性小米 - 《日本时报》 台湾原住民农民重振气候适应性小米 10 月 21 日，台湾台东的林卡夫·伊斯马哈桑 (左) 和巴努·伊斯马哈桑在台湾台东的一块田里收割油小米。台湾原住民农民曾经种植油小米，以防止主要农作物枯死，但 60 多年前，随着大米变得更加容易获得，油小米基本上从田间消失了。 |法新社-JIJI X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads 电子邮件 打印 书签故事 复制链接 台湾——原住民农民巴努·伊斯马哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 走过一片金色的高秆田
content:
台湾本土农民复兴气候适应型小米 - 日本时报
台湾本土农民复兴气候适应型小米
10 月 21 日，农民林卡夫·伊斯马哈桑（左）和巴努·伊斯马哈桑在台湾台东的一块田里收割油小米。60 多年前，随着稻米变得更加容易获得，油小米曾是台湾原住民农民为了防止主要农作物枯死而种植的油小米，基本上从田地里消失了。 |法新社-即时
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads 电子邮件 打印 书签故事 复制链接
台湾——土著农民巴努·伊斯玛哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 走过台湾东南部一片长满高秆的金色田野，用手收割一种能抵抗极端天气的古老作物的谷粒。
60 多年前，随着稻米变得更加容易获得，油小米曾由台湾原住民农民种植，以防主粮枯死。
在过去的十年里，伊斯马哈桑和他年迈的父母一直在台东县布克拉武村的布农社区努力恢复几乎被遗忘的农作物。
“我们只是希望带回许多传统的布农族作物，并在这片土地上重新种植它们，”48 岁的伊斯马哈桑在晴朗的蓝天下的油小米田里说道。
油小米，或布农语中的莳萝，是台湾特有的植物，可以在山上野生生长。
伊斯玛哈桑首先在网上了解到这种植物，然后开始自己的研究，梳理历史文献并与部落长老交谈，其中包括一位记得上次吃这种植物是在半个世纪前的妇女。
他发现，布农族农民过去常常在种植主要作物谷子的同时种植油小米，作为收成歉收或发生灾害时的“后备”。
经过多年亲自种植油小米，伊斯玛哈桑开始明白为什么他的祖先依赖这种作物。
一粒油小米种子可以长出 15 至 20 个圆锥花序，或分枝种子簇，并且茎可以自行再生，而谷子通常每粒种子长出一个圆锥花序，必须在割下后重新播种。
当极端天气或疾病爆发蹂躏他 2.2 公顷 5.4 英亩的农场时，事实证明，它比谷子更顽强。
伊斯马哈桑说，几年前一场持续了 200 多天的干旱期间，油小米“保持鲜绿色”，而其他作物却枯萎了。
台风、洪水，甚至锈病爆发也没有影响到它。
台湾中央研究院退休教授、植物遗传学专家邢月娥15年前在一个国际论坛上第一次听说了油小米。
幸不知道的是，1890 年代采集的台湾油粟标本就存放在英国皇家植物园 (Kew)。
兴带领一个研究小组在台湾东南部的山区找到了油小米，并开始研究这种鲜为人知的谷物。
10 月 21 日，台湾台东，农民巴努·伊斯马哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 将刚收获的油小米摊开在阳光下晒干。法新社-即时
她发现种子的保护性蜡涂层使其无需灌溉、化肥或杀虫剂即可生长，即使在质量较差的土地上也是如此。
它富含油、蛋白质和矿物质，可供人类和动物食用，也可用作燃料。
“它在利用阳光和水方面自然非常有效，”辛说。
“至于土壤条件，即使是在地面布满大石头的山区，它也能生长得很好。”
伊斯玛哈桑从一粒油小米开始了他的种植。家里现在收割了两次油小米

Taiwan Indigenous farmer revives climate-resilient millet - The Japan Times
Taiwan Indigenous farmer revives climate-resilient millet
Farmers Linkav Ismahasan (left) and Banu Ismahasan harvest oil millet in a field in Taitung, Taiwan, on Oct. 21. Once grown by Indigenous farmers in Taiwan in case their staple crops died, oil millet largely disappeared from fields more than 60 years ago as rice became more available. | AFP-JIJI
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link
Taiwan – Indigenous farmer Banu Ismahasan walks through a golden field of tall stalks in southeastern Taiwan, harvesting by hand the grain heads of an ancient crop resistant to extreme weather.
Once grown by Indigenous farmers in Taiwan in case their staple crops died, oil millet largely disappeared from fields more than 60 years ago as rice became more available.
Over the past decade, Ismahasan and his elderly parents have worked to revive the nearly forgotten crop in the Bunun community in Buklavu, a village surrounded by lush green mountains in Taitung county.
“We just hope to bring back many traditional Bunun crops and grow them on this land again,” Ismahasan, 48, said in his oil millet field under a clear blue sky.
Oil millet, or dill in the Bunun language, is endemic to Taiwan and can be found growing wild in the mountains.
Ismahasan first read about the plant online and then embarked on his own research, combing through historical documents and speaking to tribal elders, including a woman who recalled last eating it half a century ago.
He discovered that Bunun farmers used to grow oil millet alongside their staple crop foxtail millet as a “back-up” when harvests failed or disasters hit.
After years of growing oil millet himself, Ismahasan came to understand why his ancestors relied on the crop.
A single oil millet seed can grow 15 to 20 panicles, or branching seed clusters, and the stems regenerate on their own, while foxtail millet typically grows one panicle per seed and must be sown again after being cut.
It has also proven hardier than foxtail millet when extreme weather or disease outbreaks have ravaged his 2.2-hectare 5.4-acre farm.
During a drought several years ago that lasted more than 200 days, the oil millet “stayed bright green” while other crops withered, Ismahasan said.
Typhoons, floods and even a rust disease outbreak have not affected it either.
Hsing Yue-ie, a retired professor from Taiwan’s Academia Sinica and an expert in plant genetics, first heard of oil millet 15 years ago at an international forum.
Unbeknownst to Hsing, specimens of Taiwan oil millet collected in the 1890s were sitting in Britain’s Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew.
Hsing led a research team to find oil millet in the mountains of southeastern Taiwan and began studying the little-known cereal.
Farmer Banu Ismahasan spreads freshly harvested oil millet out to dry in the sun in Taitung, Taiwan, on Oct. 21. | AFP-JIJI
She found that the seed’s protective wax coating enabled it to grow without irrigation, fertilizers or pesticides, even on poor-quality land.
Rich in oil, protein and minerals, it can be used for human and animal consumption, as well as for fuel.
“It’s naturally very efficient at using sunlight and water,” said Hsing.
“As for soil conditions, even in mountainous areas where the ground is full of large rocks, it can still grow very well.”
Ismahasan started his crop with one panicle of oil millet. The family now harvests oil millet twice a year on a section of their property where they grow other traditional Bunun cereal crops.
Tiny and tasteless, oil millet can be used in porridge, steamed buns, bread and even popcorn.
But the family has struggled to convince other farmers to grow it because it is not yet commercially viable.
Oil millet is not only labor intensive but also significantly more expensive for consumers than rice, by far Taiwan’s most popular staple.
While the current market for oil millet is limited, Taiwan’s National Crop Germplasm Center sees value in preserving its seeds for the future, when climate change might force more farmers to consider growing the crop.
Oil millet seeds are “very precious” because of their genetic diversity and ability to adapt to the environment, said Lin Yen-yu, an assistant researcher at the center.
Seeds are kept in aluminum foil packets and stored at minus 18 degrees Celsius under low-moisture conditions where they can last for decades, Lin said.
“In the future, when cultivation methods or climate change undergo certain shifts, their value may start to be recognized and discovered,” he said. “It preserves many possibilities.”
Ismahasan said his priority for now was to get more people in his community growing and eating oil millet, bringing “it back into our everyday lives, just as it was for our elders.”
“If we don’t even eat it ourselves anymore, how can we expect to turn it into a viable business?” he said.

title: Hong Kong police chief backs Interpol 'Silver Notice' to combat illegal funds

summary: 香港警务处长支持国际刑警组织“银色通缉令”打击非法资金中国劳工公告 星期日, 15 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 香港警察局长支持国际刑警组织“银通”打击非法资金 香港警务处长周一明表示，国际刑警组织今年首次在香港举行大会之际，香港加入了国际刑警组织的“银通”试点，可以帮助打击诈骗犯罪。他还详细介绍了面部识别的推出和反欺诈工作。香港警务处处长周一明表示，准备工作正在
content:
香港警务处长支持国际刑警组织“银色通缉令”打击非法资金中国劳工公告栏
星期日, 15 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻（英文）
香港警务处长支持国际刑警组织“银色通缉令”打击非法资金
香港警务处长周一明表示，国际刑警组织大会首次在香港举行大会之际，香港今年加入的国际刑警组织“银色通缉令”试点项目可能有助于打击诈骗犯罪。他还详细介绍了面部识别的推出和反欺诈工作。
香港警务处处长周一明表示，国际刑警组织首届大会将于本月底在香港举行，筹备工作已接近完成。明在电视节目中透露，今年已进行了约十次排练和演习，对赛事的成功举办充满信心。
明强调了国际刑警组织去年推出的针对非法资金流动的“银色通缉令”试点计划。根据该计划，当一个国家或地区扣押犯罪所得并通过国际刑警组织发出“银通令”时，其他国家或地区可以采取先发制人的措施。香港今年年初加入了试点。明表示，他希望该通知能够在即将召开的大会上获得批准，并“充分利用”打击诈骗犯罪。
关于诈骗团伙，明指出，缅甸北部的一个犯罪团伙被瓦解后，这些团伙仍然集中在东盟国家，部分团伙已转移到中东和非洲。他强调国际跨境合作的必要性。涉及香港居民被引诱和拘留的案件相对减少，警方会继续与保安局和海外执法机构合作。
周三，警方的“锐眼”系统将启动面部识别功能。明表示，该系统有门槛，以确保制衡，不能随意使用。目前它的目标是犯罪和失踪人员案件。当被问及如何将系统连接到购物中心时，Ming表示连接过程必须确保数据不被泄露或被黑客攻击，这需要强大的防火墙。向更多购物中心和第三方的推广将逐步进行。他补充说，闭路电视系统有助提高香港的破案率，并大幅减少抢劫案件。

Hong Kong police chief backs Interpol 'Silver Notice' to combat illegal funds | China Labour Bulletin Board
Sunday, 15 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong police chief backs Interpol 'Silver Notice' to combat illegal funds
Hong Kong police chief Monday Ming says Interpol's 'Silver Notice' pilot, joined by Hong Kong this year, could help fight scam crimes as the Interpol general assembly meets in Hong Kong for the first time. He also details facial recognition rollout and anti-fraud efforts.
Hong Kong's Police Commissioner Monday Ming said preparations are nearly complete for the first-ever Interpol General Assembly to be held in Hong Kong at the end of this month. Speaking on a television programme, Ming revealed that around ten rehearsals and drills have been conducted this year, expressing confidence in the successful hosting of the event.
Ming highlighted the 'Silver Notice' pilot scheme launched by Interpol last year, which targets illegal fund flows. Under the scheme, when a country or region seizes criminal proceeds and issues a 'Silver Notice' through Interpol, other countries or regions can take pre-emptive measures. Hong Kong joined the pilot early this year. Ming said he hopes the notice will be approved at the upcoming assembly and 'put to good use' in combating scam crimes.
Regarding fraud gangs, Ming noted that after the dismantling of a syndicate in northern Myanmar, these groups remain concentrated in ASEAN countries, with some having moved to the Middle East and Africa. He stressed the need for international cross-border cooperation. Cases involving Hong Kong residents being lured and detained have relatively decreased, and the police will continue to work with the Security Bureau and overseas law enforcement agencies.
On Wednesday, the police's 'Sharp Eye' system will activate facial recognition functions. Ming said the system has thresholds to ensure checks and balances, and is not for casual use. It is currently aimed at crime and missing person cases. Asked about connecting the system to shopping malls, Ming said the connection process must ensure data is not leaked or hacked, requiring strong firewalls. The rollout to more malls and third parties will be gradual. He added that the CCTV system has helped raise Hong Kong's crime-solving rate and significantly reduced robbery cases.

zh_title: 习特朗普普京深圳峰会让人想起1945年雅尔塔瓜分
summary: 中美俄可能举行的峰会引发了现代雅尔塔会议的警报，三位有权势的人瓜分世界——几乎不顾乌克兰、欧洲、台湾或其他任何人。香港深水埗的一个摊位上展示着美国总统唐纳德·特朗普、中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京等人的面孔的磁铁。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。但除了历史性的拍照机会外，习近平主席、唐纳德·特朗普和弗拉基米尔·普京在 11 月 18 日至 19 日深圳 APEC 峰会上的会晤可能会实现
content:
中美俄可能举行的峰会引发了现代雅尔塔会议的警报，三位有权势的人瓜分世界——几乎不顾乌克兰、欧洲、台湾或其他任何国家。香港深水埗的一个摊位上展示着美国总统唐纳德·特朗普、中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京等人的面孔的磁铁。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。但分析人士表示，除了历史性的拍照机会之外，习近平主席、唐纳德·特朗普和弗拉基米尔·普京在 11 月 18 日至 19 日深圳 APEC 峰会上的会晤可能不会取得什么成果。势力范围 1945 年 2 月，时任美国总统富兰克林·罗斯福、英国温斯顿·丘吉尔和苏联领导人约瑟夫·斯大林在雅尔塔会面，他们制定了二战后的解决方案和欧洲新的领土边界。那次会议在雅尔塔举行，当时在苏联，现在在 2014 年被俄罗斯吞并的乌克兰部分地区举行，为苏联统治东欧和冷战奠定了基础。乌克兰总统泽伦斯基警告称，深圳可能会成为21世纪类似雅尔塔的“势力范围重新分配”。三巨头在雅尔塔会议制定了击败德国的最终计划。照片：维基共享资源。
本周在阿布扎比举行的会谈（自二月份以来的首次会谈）上，俄罗斯谈判代表推动对欧洲大陆安全架构的审查作为任何和平协议的一部分，这让乌克兰及其欧洲支持者感到不安，美国也提出了一个新框架。俄罗斯驻阿布扎比代表团团长弗拉基米尔·梅丁斯基（Vladimir Medinsky）质疑欧洲是否参与进一步谈判，从而煽动了这种担忧。哈德逊研究所的齐波拉·弗里德表示，三边关系令人恼火，因为它标志着“一些大国可以决定其他国家的安全和未来”。她告诉法新社，仅这种形式“就已经传达了一个信息，即谁重要，谁的利益可以由其他人协商”。利益分歧 然而，除了象征意义之外，利益分歧使得在深圳建立新的世界秩序的可能性不大。据报道，就连议程也仍然存在争议：俄罗斯建议会议重点关注乌克兰，特朗普推动就核武器和伊朗战争进行谈判，而中国对这两个问题都守口如瓶。北京人民大学重阳金融研究院院长王文表示，“三方的诉求差异很大，预期管理变得困难。谈判很有可能在没有突破的情况下结束。”三位领导人的意见也很少能带来进展。
例如，北京和华盛顿之间的主要争论点是贸易和人工智能技术竞赛。 自称多边主义捍卫者的北京多次表示，欧洲应该参与乌克兰和平谈判。布鲁塞尔欧盟委员会总部前悬挂着乌克兰和欧盟旗帜。资料图片：欧盟委员会。德国总统施泰因迈尔表示，在最近的一次会议上，当涉及乌克兰问题的三边会谈的想法出现时，习近平表现出了“恼怒”。 “他明确指出，这是一场欧洲冲突，欧洲人也必须参与其中，”施泰因迈尔告诉 ARD。在核裁军问题上，中国长期坚持美俄削减核裁军

【原文 English Original】
A possible China-US-Russia summit has prompted alarm of a modern-day Yalta Conference, with three powerful men carving up the world — with little regard for Ukraine, Europe and Taiwan or anyone else. Magnets showing faces of US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin, alongside others, are displayed at a stall in Sham Shui Po, Hong Kong. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. But apart from an historic photo opportunity, the meeting between Presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin at the November 18-19 APEC summit in Shenzhen will likely achieve little, analysts say. Spheres of influence When then US president Franklin D. Roosevelt, Britain’s Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin met in Yalta in February 1945, they laid out the post-WWII settlement and new territorial boundaries in Europe. That meeting in Yalta, then in the Soviet Union and now in a part of Ukraine annexed by Russia in 2014, laid out the foundations for the Soviet domination of Eastern Europe and the Cold War. Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky has raised alarm that Shenzhen could be a Yalta-like “redistribution of spheres of influence” for the 21st century. Conference of the Big Three at Yalta makes final plans for the defeat of Germany. Photo: Wikicommons. At talks in Abu Dhabi this week — the first since February — Russian negotiators rattled Ukraine and its European supporters by pushing a review of the continent’s security architecture as part of any peace deal, with the US also floating a new framework. Russia’s delegation chief in Abu Dhabi, Vladimir Medinsky, fanned such fears by questioning the inclusion of Europe in further talks. The trilateral rankles because it signals “the idea that a few great powers can decide the security and future of other countries over their heads”, according to Tsiporah Fried at the Hudson Institute. The format alone “would already send a message about who counts, and whose interests can be negotiated by others”, she told AFP. Divergent interests Beyond the symbolism, however, divergent interests make the creation of a new world order in Shenzhen unlikely. Even the agenda reportedly remains contentious: Russia has suggested the meeting focus on Ukraine, Trump has pushed for talks on nuclear weapons and the Iran war, and China has remained tight-lipped on both. “The three parties have vastly different demands, making the management of expectations difficult. There is a high probability that talks could end without a breakthrough,” according to Wang Wen, dean of the Chongyang Institute for Financial Studies at Renmin University in Beijing. There are also few issues where input from all three leaders could bring progress. The main points of contention between Beijing and Washington are trade and the AI technology race, for instance. Beijing — which presents itself as a champion of multilateralism — has repeatedly said that Europe should be part of peace negotiations over Ukraine. Ukrainian and European Union flags in front of the European Commission’s headquarters in Brussels. File photo: European Commission. German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier said that in a recent meeting, Xi showed “irritation” when the idea of the trilateral talks covering Ukraine came up. “He explicitly pointed out that this is a European conflict, in which the Europeans must also be at the table,” Steinmeier told ARD. On nuclear disarmament, China has long insisted that the US and Russia reduce their own giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its own stockpile. The summit therefore is more likely to produce minor outcomes such as crisis hotlines or some cooperation on counter-terrorism, public health, or climate change, Wang told AFP. “There is no single enemy to unite all three great powers the way that the fight against Nazi Germany united Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin,” said Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at Australian National University. “It follows that piecemeal horse-trading is in; a grand bargain is out.” However, Taiwan — which China claims — will still be watching the meeting closely, Sung said. Taiwan President Lai Ching-te. File photo: Taiwan’s Presidential Office, via Flickr. “If the Trump administration is open to abandoning one partner (Ukraine) out of convenience, then it can abandon another,” he said. A post-Shenzhen world The Trump administration has sought to reassert US dominance over the “Western hemisphere” — including by capturing Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in January — but splitting the world among great powers like it’s 1945 may not guarantee security. China has opposed the logic of Yalta — the clandestine division of spheres of influence and major powers determining the fate of other nations — “from the very beginning”, according to Renmin University’s Wang. See also: What the US midterms mean for ties with China China could allay fears of a second Yalta by using the summit to “emphasise the defence of sovereignty and support for multilateral organisations”, Wang said. If Beijing uses the meeting to insist on European inclusion in talks regarding the continent’s security, it “could, in fact, open a new window for communication between China and Europe”, he said. “The original Yalta opened the path to the Korean War and Indochina Wars in addition to various conflicts and insurgencies across Asia, Africa, and Latin America,” said Chong Ja Ian at the National University of Singapore. Any Yalta 2.0 agreement “will almost certainly run into the same kinds of issues”, Chong said.

title: Military Makes up Majority of Expulsions at Fifth Plenum
zh_title: 五中全会驱逐人员中军人占大多数
summary: 内容提要：五中全会的三分之二驱逐事件与中华人民共和国（PRC）的国防机构有关。被开除干部的背景表明，无论是专业资格还是与习近平的长期个人关系都无法提供可靠的保护以免受纪律调查。正在进行的清洗主要影响的是中国人民解放军（PLA）军队。与此同时，空军没有被驱逐，这强化了这样的评估：空军可能会在重建后的解放军最高指挥部中获得更大的影响力。正式开除
content:
内容提要：五中全会的三分之二驱逐事件与中华人民共和国（PRC）的国防机构有关。被开除干部的背景表明，无论是专业资格还是与习近平的长期个人关系都无法提供可靠的保护以免受纪律调查。正在进行的清洗主要影响的是中国人民解放军（PLA）军队。与此同时，空军没有被驱逐，这强化了这样的评估：空军可能会在重建后的解放军最高指挥部中获得更大的影响力。全会上正式开除的决定表明，无理缺席党内重大活动是政治垮台的明确信号：16名被开除的官员中有11人缺席2025年10月的四中全会，另外两人随后立即从公众视野中消失。中国反腐败监管机构正在密切关注国防工业领导人。进一步的调查可能会扰乱航空航天和造船业，给中国的国防工业基础和军事现代化带来新的挑战。中国共产党中央委员会最近召开了五中全会，重点关注党内纪律、权力集中、思想强化和人事调整（《中国简报》，11 月 3 日；IISS，11 月 4 日）。
其中一项突出进展是开除33名中央委员的党籍（IDSS报，11月4日）。其中涉及16名武装部队军官和17名文职干部，其中六人与国防国有企业关系密切（《早报》，10月30日）。尽管中央军委副主席张升民进入政治局引起了分析人士的广泛关注，但大规模驱逐前军官和国防工业领导人也同样重要，甚至更重要——揭示了对中国武装部队状况的有意义的见解。军队开除 在被开除军官名单中名列前茅的是前解放军将军、中央军委副主席张又侠。作为中越边境冲突期间的一名功勋指挥官，张在2017年至2026年担任中央军委副主席期间还一直担任政治局委员，是最高军事和民事决策机构之间的关键纽带。尽管张与习近平有着长期的关系，但他不知何故与中国领导人发生了冲突，并于 2026 年 1 月被免职并被拘留，与他在一起的还有刘振立。刘振立是一位陆军将领、战争英雄，曾在中央军委任职，并于 2022 年至 2026 年担任中国人民解放军参谋长。
中央于 2026 年 9 月首次开除张、刘的党籍，随后在五中全会上重申了这一决定（中国最高法院，9 月 21 日）继张、刘之后的是中国人民解放军海军上将王仁华，他于 2019 年至 2025 年担任中央军委政法委员会书记，负责军事司法系统和反间谍工作。王于 2025 年 10 月失踪，一切都没有发生。直到最近他被开除出中共，才听说过他（财新，2025 年 10 月 28 日）。刘青松，海军上将，2023年至2025年任东部战区政委。他与去年10月被清洗的东部战区司令员林向阳一起工作（《中国简报》，2025年11月25日）。刘就是其中之一

Executive Summary: Two thirds of the Fifth Plenum’s expulsions are tied to the national defense apparatus in the People’s Republic of China (PRC). The backgrounds of expelled cadres suggest that neither professional credentials nor longstanding personal relationships with Xi offer reliable protection against disciplinary investigations. The ongoing purge mainly affected the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) Army. The absence of Air Force expulsions, meanwhile, reinforces the assessment that the service may gain greater influence in the reconstructed PLA high command. Expulsions formalized at the plenum suggest that unjustified absence from major Party events is an unambiguous signal of political downfall: Eleven of the 16 expelled officers were absent from the Fourth Plenum in October 2025, while two others disappeared from public view immediately afterwards. Chinese anti-corruption watchdogs are keeping defense industry leaders under close scrutiny. Further investigations could disrupt the aerospace and shipbuilding sectors, creating new challenges for the PRC’s defense industrial base and military modernization. The Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) Central Committee recently concluded its Fifth Plenum, focusing on internal Party discipline, the centralization of power, ideological reinforcement, and personnel reshuffles ( China Brief , November 3; IISS , November 4). One outstanding development was the expulsion of 33 Central Committee members from the Party ( IDSS Paper , November 4). These involved 16 armed forces officers and 17 civilian cadres, six of whom were closely linked with defense state-owned enterprises ( Zaobao , October 30). Although the promotion of Central Military Commission (CMC) Vice Chairman Zhang Shengmin (张升民) to the Politburo attracted considerable analyst attention, the mass expulsion of former military officers and defense industry leaders is of equal, if not greater, importance—revealing meaningful insights on the state of the Chinese armed forces. Armed Forces Expulsions At the top of the list of expelled military officers is former People’s Liberation Army (PLA) general and CMC Vice Chairman Zhang Youxia (张又侠). As a decorated commander during the Sino-Vietnamese border conflict, Zhang also served on the Politburo throughout his tenure as CMC vice chairman from 2017–2026, serving as a critical link between top military and civilian decision-making organs. Despite his longstanding ties with Xi, Zhang somehow ran afoul of the Chinese leader and was removed and detained in January 2026, alongside Liu Zhenli (刘振立), a fellow Army general and war hero who served on the CMC and as the PLA chief of staff from 2022–2026. The Central Committee first expelled Zhang and Liu from the Party in September 2026, before it reaffirmed the decision at the Fifth Plenum ( China Supreme Court , September 21) Following Zhang and Liu is PLA Navy admiral Wang Renhua (王仁华), who served as secretary of the CMC political and legal affairs commission from 2019–2025, in charge of the military justice system and counterespionage. Wang disappeared in October 2025 and nothing was heard of him until his recent expulsion from the CCP ( Caixin , October 28, 2025). Liu Qingsong (刘青松) is a Navy admiral who served as the political commissar of the Eastern Theater Command from 2023–2025. He worked with the disgraced Eastern Theater Command Commander Lin Xiangyang (林向阳), who was purged in October last year ( China Brief , November 25, 2025). Liu was one of at least 18 officers absent at the Fourth Plenum in October 2025 ( Sing Tao Daily , October 27, 2025; BBC , November 7, 2025). His whereabouts remained unknown until his expulsion at the Fifth Plenum. Army general Huang Ming (黄铭) first vanished from public view in July 2025 and was absent at the subsequent Fourth Plenum. The commander of the Northern Theater Command from 2024–2025, Huang was once regarded as a promising leader within the Army ( Zaobao , August 3, 2024). His expulsion at the Fifth Plenum, however, sealed his fate. Li Qiaoming (李桥铭) was another elite Army general with a long list of professional accomplishments. He rose from a simple soldier to become the fourth commander of the PLA Army in 2022. Yet Li was missing in action during the Fourth Plenum last year and was booted out of the National People’s Congress (NPC) in February 2026 ( Xinhua , February 26). His expulsion from the CCP at the Fifth Plenum made him the third Army commander to be purged since the post was created in 2015 amid changes to the military’s organizational structure known as the “Deepening National Defense and Military Reform” (深化国防和军队改革). Army general Li Wei (李伟) was the third political commissar of the now-disbanded Strategic Support Force and then became the first political commissar of the Information Support Force, founded in 2024 to succeed the Strategic Support Force’s cyber capabilities ( Zaobao , April 20, 2024; China Brief, April 26, 2024 [ a ], [ b ]). Like Li Qiaoming, Li Wei failed to attend the Fourth Plenum and was removed from the NPC in February 2026. He was formally expelled from the Party at the Fifth Plenum. Zhang Hongbing (张红兵) spent most of his career in the PLA Army before transferring to the People’s Armed Police in 2022 as its political commissar, attaining the rank of general. He disappeared from public view for most of 2025, including the Fourth Plenum, and was expelled from the Party at the Fifth Plenum ( Zaobao , December 24, 2025). Wang Haijiang (汪海江) was regarded as a capable Army officer who fought in the Sino-Vietnamese border conflict ( China Brief , June 7). He spent over a decade serving at senior PLA posts in Xinjiang and Tibet before becoming the Western Theater Command commander in 2021. He did not attend the Fourth Plenum in October 2025 and was expelled from the Party at the Fifth Plenum. The same fate befell Army lieutenant general Yang Cheng (杨诚), the political commissar of the Xinjiang military district from 2020–2025 who most likely maintained working relations with Wang Haijiang ( Caixin , April 6, 2021). Three former heads of CMC departments were also expelled following their absence from last year’s Fourth Plenum. They were Army lieutenant general Wang Peng (王鹏), who headed the CMC training and administration department from 2021–2025; Army lieutenant general Liu Faqing (刘发庆), who led the CMC national defense mobilization department from 2021–2025; and Navy vice admiral Zhao Xiaozhe (赵晓哲), who previously oversaw the CMC science and technology department. Separately, Army lieutenant general Zhang Lin (张林), director of the CMC logistics support department from 2022–2025, was removed from the NPC last October and expelled at the Fifth Plenum ( Zaobao , October 16, 2025). Last but not least, Army lieutenant generals Zhong Shaojun (钟绍军) and Fang Yongxiang (方永祥) were both considered confidants of Xi. Zhong assisted Xi since the latter’s tenure in Zhejiang in the early 2000s ( VOA , August 29). After Xi came to power, he brought Zhong into the PLA as a senior colonel, despite having no military experience, to manage the crucial CMC chairman’s office that supported Xi’s daily work schedule ( China Brief , September 14). Zhong subsequently became director of the CMC general office that provided administrative and logistical support to all CMC members, before eventually serving as political commissar of the National Defense University. He vanished in October 2025 and was removed from the NPC in August 2026, prior to his expulsion from the Party in October ( Zaobao , October 29). Fang succeeded Zhong in leading both the CMC chairman’s office and CMC general office, indicating a high level of trust that Xi had in him ( SCMP , October 26, 2024). Like many previously mentioned officers, Fang failed to attend the Fourth Plenum, with no news regarding his whereabouts until his expulsion from the CCP at the recent Fifth Plenum. Defense Industry Expulsions Other than military officers, Sun Shaopin (孙绍骋), former minister of veterans affairs from 2018–2022, was also expelled from the Party ( Caixin , January 29). Moreover, one third of the 17 civilian cadres expelled at the Fifth Plenum were associated with state-owned defense enterprises. At the top of the expulsion list was Lei Fanpei (雷凡培). He had a long career in the country’s aerospace industry, rising from an ordinary designer to become chairman of the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC). From 2018–2022, Lei was the chairman of China State Shipbuilding Corporation (CSSC) ( World Ships , October 31). From 2022–2025, Lei served as the deputy director at the Office of Central Military-Civil Fusion Development Commission (中央军民融合发展委员会办公室) ( Zaobao , October 31, 2024). Despite being an experienced technocrat and crucial link between defense companies and policymakers, Lei was expelled from the Party at the Fifth Plenum. Several other senior leaders from the defense sector were expelled at the same time. They include former chairman of the China National Nuclear Corporation Yu Jianfeng (余剑锋); former chairman of CASC Yuan Jie (袁洁), who was removed in 2024 likely in connection with the Rocket Force investigations that year ( Radio Free Asia , April 15, 2024); Zhang Zhongyang (张忠阳), former chairman of CASC and head of the China Academy of Launch Vehicle Technology, the country’s largest research, development, and production institution for carrier rockets and missile systems ( Zaobao , January 30, 2024); Wen Gang (温刚), former chairman of Norinco and CSSC ( Caixin , October 30); and Jin Donghan (金东寒), an engine and marine propulsion research specialist and former president of Shanghai University and Tianjin University. Jin spent decades researching engines for the PRC’s defense industry and led the CSSC’s Shanghai Marine Diesel Engine Research Institute that specializes in marine diesel and gas engines, power systems, electrical and automation systems, and energy equipment ( 163 , January 15). Scope of Purge Shows Inter-Service Political Priorities As the largest PLA service, the Army predominated among those expelled, accounting for 11 of the 16 military officers. The Navy follows with three officers, Information Support Force and the People’s Armed Police each account for one. Neither the Air Force nor Rocket Force saw any expulsions this time. While the lack of Rocket Force expulsions may be linked to the broad purges that decimated its top leadership in 2023 and the subsequent years, the absence of Air Force expulsions again highlights this service as the least affected by the purges so far. This reinforces the author’s previous assessment that the Air Force is set to gain influence within the reconstructed PLA high command, as its senior leadership remains comparatively intact ( The Diplomat , August 11). The professional backgrounds of expelled officers also reveal important patterns in the direction of the purge. Military officers with extensive command experience constitute seven cases while political commissars account for six, followed by three defense technocrats. This shows that the commanders and commissars of major PLA organizations are most at risk. The authorities appear to make no distinction between commanders or commissars when conducting investigations. In comparison, defense technocrats, who tend to stay in the background, seem to be less affected by the current campaign. Interestingly, three expelled officers had close personal ties with Xi, with relations dating back years, if not decades. But this did not save them from being purged, indicating that Xi does not tolerate any malfeasance or signs of disloyalty among military officers, regardless of their personal relations with him. Fourth Plenum Absences as a Potential Purge Indicator Another recurring theme is the connection between the expelled and the Fourth Plenum. Out of 16 officers expelled at the Fifth Plenum, 11 were absent from the Fourth Plenum in October 2025, with two more—Wang Renhua and Zhong Shaojun—disappearing from public view immediately after the gathering. This suggests that these 13 officers had likely been detained and placed under investigation around the time of the Fourth Plenum. This sequence teaches us that absence from key Party meetings is an early warning sign of political trouble and missing individuals are likely to end up as purge victims. It is worth noting that several other officers absent from the Fourth Plenum have not yet been expelled. They include Commander of the Southern Theater Command Wu Ya’nan (吴亚男); Political Commissar of the Central Theater Command Xu Deqing (徐德清); Commander of the PLA Navy Hu Zhongming (胡中明), and Political Commissar of the PLA Rocket Force Xu Xisheng (徐西盛) ( Sing Tao Daily , October 27, 2025; BBC , November 7, 2025). Despite having no news and public appearance since the Fourth Plenum, events at the Fifth Plenum suggest that they have met their downfall. Turning to the defense industry, the affiliations of the expelled executives reveal a clear concentration of those associated with CASC and CSSC. Others were linked to the China National Nuclear Corporation, Norinco, and key research institutions developing missiles and marine engines. There may be parallels between the depth of corruption within these corporations and the quality of their equipment, echoing concerns previously raised about Rocket Force vulnerabilities ( CNA , January 11, 2024). As investigations are likely to expand in these sectors, the disruptions could have negative consequences for the PRC’s defense industrial base and military modernization. Conclusion The armed forces and defense industry cadres constitute a two-third majority of Fifth Plenum expulsions, an extraordinary development when personnel involved in national defense only account for a minority within the entire Party-state elite. While the rise of CMC Vice Chairman Zhang Shengmin reestablished formal communications between the Politburo and the PLA, the Fifth Plenum’s expulsions offer broader insights into the state of the PLA. As Xi reconstructs the high command, the Fifth Plenum reminds us that trust between the commander-in-chief and his generals remains low ( The Diplomat , July 6). While it is not difficult to appoint new people to top posts, building confidence and rapport is a long-term project that might be undermined by frequent leadership instability. title: Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China: White House
zh_title: 特朗普、习近平、普京将在中国举行历史性会晤：白宫
summary: 白宫周五表示，唐纳德·特朗普、弗拉基米尔·普京和习近平将于下周在深圳举行的峰会上举行美国、俄罗斯和中国领导人之间的首次三方会晤。 2026 年 7 月 6 日星期一，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在椭圆形办公室举行的特朗普账户启动活动中敲响了纽约证券交易所和纳斯达克的开盘钟。照片：Joyce N. Boghosian，来自 Flickr。特朗普希望在周四的三边会谈中讨论削减核武库的问题，并且还将提及他在伊朗的战争，但预计他不会讨论俄罗斯
content:
白宫周五表示，唐纳德·特朗普、弗拉基米尔·普京和习近平将于下周在深圳举行的峰会上举行美国、俄罗斯和中国领导人之间的首次三方会晤。 2026 年 7 月 6 日星期一，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在椭圆形办公室举行的特朗普账户启动活动中敲响了纽约证券交易所和纳斯达克的开盘钟。照片：Joyce N. Boghosian，来自 Flickr。美国官员表示，特朗普希望在周四的三边会谈中讨论削减核武库的问题，并且还将提及他在伊朗的战争，但预计他不会讨论俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争。白宫发言人奥利维亚·威尔士告诉记者，三位领导人将在中国南方城市亚太经合组织峰会期间会面。 “总统已明确表示，除其他议题外，他将讨论世界范围内核武器的削减。特朗普总统认为，这种扩散非常危险，”威尔士说。美国官员表示，主导特朗普第二个总统任期的主要冲突之一将成为焦点，但另一个则不会。一位不愿透露姓名的美国高级官员在电话中对记者表示：“我认为总统确实打算在与习近平和普京的三边会议上讨论伊朗问题。” 2026 年 5 月 20 日，中国国家主席习近平在北京人民大会堂。照片：克里姆林宫。
这位官员补充说，华盛顿与基辅和莫斯科有“完全不同的轨道”谈判，旨在结束乌克兰战争。他指的是美国特使最近几天与普京和乌克兰总统泽连斯基进行的会谈。“中国实际上并不是该轨道的一部分，因此在那里讨论乌克兰问题似乎并不合适，”该官员补充道。官员们表示，特斯拉和 Space X 的老板埃隆·马斯克将陪同特朗普访华，但不会参与与习近平和普京的会面。特朗普周四还将与中国国家主席举行双边工作午餐和会晤，这是自美国总统去年重新掌权以来的第四次会面。但特朗普没有计划与普京进行单独的一对一会谈。官员们表示，除其他话题外，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋因与一名所谓的中国间谍有染而辞职的问题预计不会出现在特朗普与习近平的会晤中。 2026 年 5 月 20 日，中国国家主席习近平（左）在北京人民大会堂欢迎俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京。照片：克里姆林宫。另一位美国高级官员表示：“英伟达的情况实际上不会对此次访问产生任何影响。”美国也不打算讨论敏感芯片技术的出口管制，而这正是英伟达丑闻的核心。 “我们不就美国的出口管制进行谈判。
第二位官员表示：“这些都是我们在政府中制定的国家安全问题……我们不希望它出现在我们在那里与中国人的任何对话中。”特朗普将于周一离开华盛顿，周二抵达菲律宾参加东南亚国家联盟（ASEAN）峰会，然后前往深圳。
